subject: Chemistry
solution:
Molar mass of x: $M = 2 \times \text{VD} = 2 \times 47 = 94\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
Number of C atoms: $\dfrac{0.766 \times 94}{12} \approx 6$
Number of H atoms: $\dfrac{0.0638 \times 94}{1} \approx 6$
O makes up the rest: $94 - 72 - 6 = 16\ \mathrm{g}$, i.e. 1 O atom. So x is $\mathrm{C_6H_6O}$, which is phenol.
With $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and NaOH at $120^\circ\mathrm{C}$ under pressure, then $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$, phenol undergoes the Kolbe–Schmitt reaction. So y is salicylic acid (o-hydroxybenzoic acid). Its phenolic –OH gives a violet colour with neutral $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$.
(A) Salicylic acid ($pK_a \approx 3$) is a stronger acid than $\mathrm{H_2CO_3}$. It dissolves in $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ and releases $\mathrm{CO_2}$ gas, so A is correct.
(B) Phenol ($pK_a \approx 10$) is a much weaker acid than salicylic acid ($pK_a \approx 3$). So B is incorrect.
(C) Both phenol and salicylic acid are acidic enough to dissolve in NaOH, so C is correct.
(D) Both are aromatic compounds with a high C:H ratio, so both burn with a sooty flame. D is correct.
Answer: (B)
